intro.markdown:
A scope question runs through today's commits across three repos. In `rich-js`, nine demos stopped being wired through an iframe harness and became a single `main.ts` each — same program, two entry files: one for the card in the browser, one for the terminal. The library is imported by its published names, not by relative paths. One contract, two homes.

Over in `cc-candybar`, the config stopped replacing itself on the way up. A project file now layers over the user file; every file found is a layer, and a durable click refuses to write what a layer above would hide, naming that layer. Plugins arrived in the same shape: every name a plugin declares lives under `plugins.<plugin>.`, so a drop only ever owns names under it.

In `links-issue-tracker`, a follow-up stopped being filed under the ticket it followed up. It's filed beside it now, with its own `follows_up` column — the link is a fact about the pair, not a tree position.

Brandon merged each of them in order, without pointing out they rhymed.

## Recent Engineering Work

*Updated October 13, 2026*

### Last 24 Hours

- `brandon-fryslie/rich-js` — docs card epic concludes — eight demos (rich-markup-plugins, rich-viewport, themes-and-color-studio, rich-config, rich-template-bindings, rich-explore, rich-dash, claude-sessions) each collapsed to a single `main.ts` entry, library imported by its published names, Node and browser hosts sharing one contract ([#363](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/rich-js/pull/363)–[#370](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/rich-js/pull/370)); terminal-host demo replaces the BrowserTerminalHost harness, run on NodeTerminalHost for the card and BrowserTerminalHost for the embed ([#371](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/rich-js/pull/371)); iframe demo shell deleted — `demos.json`, `_browser-shell` templates and `demos:build` gone, `demoNames()` the one list the sidebar, routes, Demos index and e2e gate read ([#372](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/rich-js/pull/372)) ([commits](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/rich-js/commits?author=brandon-fryslie&since=2026-10-12)).
- `promptctl/cc-candybar` — plugins epic — apps ship segments as plugin definitions a config lists, data lives in a watched JSON file the app rewrites, every plugin name namespaced under `plugins.<plugin>.` so a drop only owns names under it ([#319](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-candybar/pull/319)); a watched file whose directories appear after load is read when written, nearestWatchTarget re-arms one level deeper as each missing directory appears ([#320](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-candybar/pull/320)); a project config layers over the user config instead of replacing it, every file found a layer merged through the bundled default, a durable click refusing to write what a layer above would hide ([#321](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-candybar/pull/321)); installed plugins discovered from `$XDG_DATA_DIRS`, `$XDG_DATA_HOME` and `<repo>/.cc-candybar/plugins` with the folder's name as the plugin's ([#322](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-candybar/pull/322)); each plugin checked by its own declarations, not the full validateConfig — 65 ms per load down to 1.2 ms ([#323](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-candybar/pull/323)) ([commits](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-candybar/commits?author=brandon-fryslie&since=2026-10-12)).

Real HID devices through the pqrs DriverKit extension — no event taps, no Accessibility grant. 262 commits over the past month, 74 this week. Install one-command landed — one command takes a bare Mac to a running hands, Claude Code's first-run questions and login asked in-line, the plugin installs from a local marketplace in hands' own home so the accept-this-marketplace prompt stops gating an unattended run ([#273](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-hands/pull/273)–[#276](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-hands/pull/276), [#278](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-hands/pull/278), [#282](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-hands/pull/282), [#291](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-hands/pull/291)). `hands.app` runs hands and holds its macOS grants (gated to a live subscription), a setup window asks each permission in turn before hands runs, and the app never asks to be the active app so a launch does not take focus ([#285](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-hands/pull/285), [#289](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-hands/pull/289)). Setup decisions moved into a `HandsLogic` Swift package tested against a Privacy fake, and the twelve pytest paths that raised a real setup window on every run are gone ([#292](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-hands/pull/292), [#293](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-hands/pull/293), [#294](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-hands/pull/294)). Voice — tell the user's voice from someone else's in the room, named voiceprints with only the owner acting ([#277](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-hands/pull/277), [#279](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-hands/pull/279), [#280](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-hands/pull/280)). ### [low-talker](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/low-talker) **Swift** Local push-to-talk dictation for macOS with a chord-selected command layer. 179 commits over the past month, none this week — the arc has settled. Earlier in the month the streaming arc landed — a press is decoded while the key is down, confirmed words commit while the press is open, dictation stays in the app its first words reached, streamed commits wait for settled punctuation ([#150](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/low-talker/pull/150)–[#153](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/low-talker/pull/153)); command mode leaves the code — an utterance becomes one thing, its text at the cursor ([#160](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/low-talker/pull/160)); a HUD with listening/transcribing, Open at Login, Fn/Globe as the chord ([#161](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/low-talker/pull/161)–[#168](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/low-talker/pull/168)); audio under the audible floor answered as nothing said, `verbose_json` serves `avg_logprob` and `compression_ratio`, and an install from huggingface.co records the sizes the hub lists for the revision so a truncated file is fetched again instead of certified ([#169](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/low-talker/pull/169)–[#171](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/low-talker/pull/171)). ### [rich-js](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/rich-js) **TypeScript · MIT** A port of Python's Rich to TypeScript — markup, tables, trees, syntax, progress, tracebacks, Live, and an App runtime that routes focus and the pointer. 163 commits over the past month, 37 this week. The docs card epic concluded — static examples became editable cards running in the browser, with output re-rendered client-side, keyboard input, file tabs, slider playgrounds, and edits reaching a running program without restarting it ([#351](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/rich-js/pull/351)–[#362](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/rich-js/pull/362)); then every demo collapsed to a single `main.ts` entry importing the library by its published names, with a terminal-host demo replacing the old BrowserTerminalHost harness, and the iframe demo shell deleted — `demoNames()` is the one list the sidebar, routes, Demos index and e2e gate read ([#363](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/rich-js/pull/363)–[#372](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/rich-js/pull/372)). New repo last week, 65 commits since. Concurrent deploys rebuild from the probed tip instead of rebasing, deploy concurrency is keyed per version slot, token kept out of process args and `.git/config`, publish retries bounded by a 10-minute deadline ([#1](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/gh-pages-multiplexer/pull/1)–[#5](https://github.com/brandon-fryslie/gh-pages-multiplexer/pull/5)).
